$comment: content/docs/social/copy.mdx's tables as data. That page is the doctrine and stays the doctrine — this file is only the part a machine can execute, and it must never say anything copy.mdx does not. Two implementations read it (src/lib/craft.ts for the app, scripts/lib/craft.mjs for the CLI and the drain) because a .mjs cannot import TS; craft.test.ts pins them byte-identically. Severity follows copy.mdx's own split: its `reject list` is 'auto-fail, no discussion' so those are `fail`, and its register ladder + checks 3/5 are judgment so those are `warn`. Checks 1's 'is this a pain or a promise', 2's 'cut it at any sentence boundary', and 4 'Scene' are NOT here — the first two need a reader and the third needs evidence, not a regex. `reason` maps every rule onto the five reviewer-facing DISMISS_REASONS in src/components/root/social/knobs.ts, so a machine refusal and a human dismissal speak one vocabulary.
$comment_shortForm: copy.mdx: 'Under 400 only for X.' X is not in scope for the slice, so arMinCharsShortForm applies only when a caller passes channel=x.

openerBans.$comment: copy.mdx check 1, matched against the first line only. These are brand-independent.

$comment_brandOpenerNames: copy.mdx check 1: 'Never opens with the brand name' — its OWN name. Keyed by the registry id in src/components/root/social/products.ts, and only the brand being written is checked. Checking all five would flag `مكان واحد` on a hogwarts post, and `في مكان واحد` is in this file's own preferredAr list. Both scripts per brand, because the transliteration rule means Arabic prose says هوجورتس and an opener is a violation either way. The note lives OUTSIDE the object so every value is a string[] and the map needs no cast.

wordlist.$comment: copy.mdx's wordlist table, verbatim in both columns. `use` is printed in the failure message so a refusal carries its own fix. Arabic is matched as a substring — JS \b does not work on Arabic script — so terms are chosen long enough not to fire inside an innocent word.

engineeringAr.$comment: copy.mdx reject list: 'Engineering vocabulary carried into Arabic.' These are the exact three it names, plus the two the 2026-08-05 failure actually shipped.

passiveAr.$comment: copy.mdx's wordlist bans `يتم + مصدر` outright, so يتم is a fail. The ladder's other rung-1 markers are judgment, so they warn — the page is explicit that passive is RIGHT when the object is the topic (الدرجة تُرصد مرة واحدة is called good), which no regex can tell.

preferredAr.$comment: copy.mdx: 'the register's own vocabulary, mined from the copy that works.' Check 3 warns when a draft carries none of these — an abstraction with no object a reader can see.
